items.title: Bipartisan Senate Deal Answers Manufacturers’ Call for Permitting Reform

items.summary: Whitehouse's opening statement at the Jan. 28 EPW hearing says he wants strong bipartisan permitting reform but that a trust problem with the administration's behavior must be solved first.

quote.text: The responsibility for resuscitating permitting reform rests now upon the executive branch, upon credible confidence that the nonsense will stop
quote.speaker: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse

items.author: Shelley Moore Capito
items.title: Chairman Capito Highlights Consensus on Need for NEPA and Permitting Reform Legislation
items.summary: Capito's release on the Feb. 19, 2025 EPW hearing, where she questioned industry and organization witnesses about project delays and the need for legislation on federal environmental review.

items.author: Drew Maloney
items.title: EEI Statement on House Passage of the SPEED Act
items.summary: EEI's president and CEO calls House passage of the SPEED Act an important first step toward cutting red tape and lowering customer costs, and says EEI will keep working on a more predictable and durable permitting system for all energy forms.

quote.text: The House passage of the Speed Act is an important first step toward cutting red tape, lowering customer costs, and delivering reliable, affordable electricity to American families and businesses.
quote.speaker: Drew Maloney, EEI President and CEO

items.author: Alex Music
items.title: Bipartisan drive for permitting reform grows, but outlook is still murky
items.summary: Reports Republicans and Democrats share ground on permitting certainty while recent Trump administration moves impede negotiations.
